clusters.neutral_headline: Sleep paralysis: when you’re awake, but can’t move – or even breathe | Letters

items.title: Sleep paralysis: when you’re awake, but can’t move – or even breathe | Letters
items.standfirst: Readers recount their terrifying experiences of sleep paralysis in response to an article by Amy FlemingI experienced sleep paralysis and hypnagogic hallucinations from childhood and into adulthood, with the episodes only waning in my 30s (Touch of evil: the terrifying truth about sleep paralysis, 11 November). I never spoke about them to anyone.I experienced hallucinations in the form of severe perspective distortion (oversized bed and rooms) and full hallucinations/dream states, auditory hallucinations (screaming and loud thumping) and, of course, paralysis. I didn’t know at what point I was asleep or if I had woken and could easily slip back into a hypnagogic state. I only became aware of this state as an adult, having been referred to a psychiatrist on an unrelated matter. Continue reading...

clusters.title: Menopause symptoms aren’t always taken seriously. These female lawmakers plan to change that
clusters.neutral_headline: Menopause symptoms aren’t always taken seriously. These female lawmakers...

items.title: Menopause symptoms aren’t always taken seriously. These female lawmakers plan to change that
items.standfirst: From Utah to Louisiana, US states are making menopause care more affordable and accessible for midlife womenMelissa Shusterman was desperate for help with her menopausal symptoms: body aches, lethargy and brain fog, which she described as feeling “not myself”. The Pennsylvania state representative saw a gynecologist, a physical therapist, a chiropractor and a urologist. One doctor gave her lubricant, even though she’d already explained to him that sex was not the problem. (“Have you seen my husband?” she quipped.)“I am more than lubrication,” Shusterman said. “I am a dynamic, smart, hardworking woman who wants to continue to feel good, so I can join my contemporaries, get back to work, and change things.” Continue reading...
